about.title: Santa Maria Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: A hospital stay or clinic visit in Santa Maria is supposed to leave you better off, not worse. Most of the time it does. Occasionally, though, a diagnosis is missed, a medication is dosed wrong, or a surgical step is skipped, and a family on the Central Coast is left sorting through what happened and why. California's MICRA rules shape every one of these cases. You generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm to file, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Before suing, a 90-day notice must go to each provider. Non-economic damages are capped, though that cap rises every year, and nearly every claim needs a qualified medical expert to explain how the standard of care was breached. A poor result by itself is not malpractice; the question is whether a reasonably careful provider would have acted differently. We review Santa Maria medical malpractice claims directly and can answer that question honestly.

items.question: My treatment in Santa Maria did not go well. Does that mean I have a malpractice case?
items.answer: Not by itself. California law separates a bad outcome from negligent care, and only the latter supports a claim. We typically have a qualified medical expert compare what your providers did against what a reasonably careful provider in the same specialty would have done. If that review shows a breach that caused harm, you may have a case.

items.question: How long do I have to file in Santa Barbara County?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered, or should have discovered, the injury, and in no event more than three years from the date of the injury. You must also serve a 90-day notice of intent on each provider before filing suit. Because these windows overlap, it is wise to speak with us well before the one-year mark.

items.question: What does it cost to talk with our team?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle medical malpractice on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.
